claim: Income Tax Ordinance s.116A: a resident individual with foreign income of not less than USD 10,000, OR foreign assets of not less than USD 100,000, must furnish a foreign income and assets statement.
note: Quoted verbatim from FBR. Basis of the US-LLC-as-declarable-foreign-asset angle.

claim: s.154A(1)(a) makes PSEB registration a statutory condition: the reduced rate applies to exports of computer software / IT services / IT enabled services 'where the exporter is registered with and duly certified by the Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB)'.
source: Income Tax Ordinance 2001, amended to 31.07.2025, p.329-330
note: PSEB wording substituted by Finance Act 2022.

claim: First Schedule Part III Division IVA: 0.25% of proceeds for PSEB-registered exporters of computer software/IT/ITeS; 1% of proceeds in any other case.
source: Income Tax Ordinance 2001, First Schedule Part III Div IVA, p.529
note: Core fact of the freelancer cluster. NOTE: the 1% 'any other case' rate in Div IVA is for services; the Finance Act 2026 separately raised the s.154 EXPORT OF GOODS rate to 1.25%. So PSEB-registered IT export is 0.25% vs 1% for other services (4x) and vs 1.25% for goods (5x). Do not conflate the two comparisons.

claim: The statute as amended to 31.07.2025 limits the 0.25% rate to 'tax years 2024 up to tax year 2026'. Widely-published claims of an extension to 30 June 2029 are NOT in this text.
source: Income Tax Ordinance 2001, First Schedule Part III Div IVA
note: MATERIAL. Secondary sources (urcapk, filing.pk, cssprep) claim FTR extended to 2029, likely via Finance Act 2026 which post-dates this PDF. MUST resolve against Finance Act 2026 before publishing any sunset date.

claim: s.154A(2): the deduction is a final tax only if (a) a return has been filed, (b) withholding tax statements for the relevant year have been filed where required, and (c) sales tax returns under federal or provincial law have been filed where required (with a proviso disapplying (c) for clause (a) exporters).
note: The compliance conditions nobody explains. Direct content opportunity.

claim: The '80% of export proceeds remitted through normal banking channels' condition appears in the Ordinance only inside a clause OMITTED by the Finance Act 2022 (former Second Schedule Pt I cl.(133), which ran to 30 June 2025).
source: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 footnote, Second Schedule
note: Research briefs treated the 80% rule as a live s.154A condition. In this text it belongs to a repealed exemption. Verify current status before publishing.

claim: SECP operates 'eZfile' as a live platform with its own user registration video, incorporation video, annual filing video, support page and user manual, linked from the SECP homepage.
note: Competitor guides still describing 'eServices' are stale. Confirms the timeboxed opportunity.

claim: SBP FE Circular No. 01 of 11 July 2024 revised Para 13(II)A, Chapter 20 of the Foreign Exchange Manual to introduce a new Equity Investment Abroad category for export-oriented companies in the IT sector; removed prior bank-designation for exporters using Exporters Special Foreign Currency Accounts; permitted IT export companies to acquire shareholding in entities abroad; and relaxed the one-entity-per-jurisdiction restriction for them.
note: MAJOR. Directly answers 'can a Pakistani IT company legally own a foreign entity'. No competitor covers this. Fetched with scrapling StealthyFetcher after plain curl was blocked.

claim: Equity Investment Abroad by residents is governed by Para 13, Chapter 20 of the SBP Foreign Exchange Manual.
note: The citation competitors omit entirely.

claim: Trade Marks Rules 2004 First Schedule, as substituted w.e.f. 09-03-2019 by SRO under s.132 Trade Marks Ordinance 2001: TM-1 application to register in one class PKR 3,000; TM-11 registration of a trade mark PKR 9,000; TM-12 renewal PKR 15,000; TM-12 late-renewal additional fee PKR 900; TM-13 restoration PKR 3,000; TM-5 notice of opposition PKR 9,000; TM-6 counter-statement PKR 1,500.
source: Gazette notification, Ministry of Commerce & Textile, March 2019

claim: The trademark fee schedule in force dates from a 2019 revision (effective 09-03-2019); no later revision notification is linked from IPO Pakistan's trademark fee page.
source: ipo.gov.pk trademark fee page link inventory
note: Means the 2019 figures are current, not stale. Worth stating explicitly since readers assume fees have risen.

claim: The Finance Act 2026 extended the reduced 0.25% rate for PSEB-registered exporters of IT and IT-enabled services from tax year 2026 to tax year 2029.
source: KPMG Taseer Hadi & Co, A Brief of Finance Act 2026 (July 2026), Division IVA commentary
note: RESOLVES finding s154a-sunset-2026. The Ordinance PDF was amended only to 31.07.2025 and therefore predates this. Both records kept: the sunset one documents why the discrepancy existed.

claim: The Finance Act 2026 inserted new Division IIIAB providing withholding tax at 5% on amounts received by a person through social media platforms, under new section 154B.
note: Confirms the creator/influencer tax at statute level and names the section (154B), which the earlier secondary sources did not. Directly relevant to the platform-monetization service line.

claim: The Finance Act 2026 raised the export-of-goods withholding rate under s.154 from 1% to 1.25%.
note: Widens the PSEB gap: IT exports 0.25% vs goods 1.25% is now 5x, not 4x. Sharpens the PSEB registration argument.

claim: The Finance Act 2026 prescribed a single 2.75% advance tax rate on sale or transfer of immovable property under s.236C, irrespective of the amount of consideration.
note: CHECK against lib/tax/property.ts: if the property calculators still model slabbed 236C rates they may be out of date.

claim: The Finance Act 2026 prescribed a single 1.25% advance tax rate on purchase of immovable property under s.236K, irrespective of the fair market value.

source: KPMG Brief of Finance Act 2026, Division XXVII

claim: BarrioVibe's property calculator matches the Finance Act 2026 position on both s.236C (flat 2.75% seller) and s.236K (flat 1.25% filer buyer, banded non-filer).

source: Microsoft On the Issues, State of Global AI Diffusion (7 May 2026)

claim: Pakistan was removed from the FATF grey list on 21 October 2022 after four years.

claim: SECP registered 43,559 new companies in FY2025-26, up 24% YoY, against a national total of 301,615. IT & e-commerce was the largest sector at 8,700 new companies; trading 6,615 (fastest growth, 41%); services 5,368; real estate & construction 4,042. 1,014 foreign companies with 1,512 foreign shareholders.
source: The Nation (4 Jul 2026), corroborated by Business Recorder
note: Ranked addressable market, not a guess. IT & e-commerce being the largest sector is the strongest argument for the convergence positioning.

claim: Companies Act 2017 s.130: every company files an annual return once a year, on Form A (with share capital) or Form B (without). Listed companies file within 30 days of the AGM, extendable to 45 by the registrar; other companies within 30 days of the AGM. Under s.197, Form 29 reports appointment, cessation or change of officers within 15 days. Under s.437 a foreign company files Form 45.
source: SECP, Annual Returns (Form A/B and Form 29), fetched with scrapling StealthyFetcher
note: CORRECTS the agent's version on two points. (1) The 30/45-day split is listed vs other companies, NOT private vs public. (2) There ARE exemptions where particulars are unchanged: an SMC or a private company with paid-up capital of not more than PKR 3 million need not file Form A/B at all, and other companies need only notify the registrar of no change. The claim of 'no exemption for dormant or newly registered companies' was wrong. The 120-day AGM rule is not stated on this page and still needs the Companies Act s.132 text.

claim: Pakistan's Digital Presence Proceeds Tax on FOREIGN digital providers was suspended via SRO 1366(I)/2025 effective 1 July 2025, but DOMESTIC e-commerce obligations were not suspended: mandatory sales tax registration for e-commerce providers from August 2025, and withholding of 1% on digital/bank payments and 2% on cash on delivery collected by banks and couriers.
source: ITIF; VATupdate; Profit by Pakistan Today; FBR SRO PDF exists
note: HIGH VALUE. Most coverage conflates the suspended foreign tax with the live domestic obligations. A correction piece is defensible and currently mis-served. Verify the 1%/2% against enacted Finance Act 2025 text first: the figures come from instruments at different stages.

claim: UAE Small Business Relief (revenue at or below AED 3,000,000) expires 31 December 2026. QFZP status requires all seven conditions including audited IFRS statements; the de minimis for non-qualifying revenue is 5% of total revenue or AED 5 million, whichever is lower. Late FTA registration penalty AED 10,000.
note: A dated cliff about 16 months out affecting every client set up in the UAE. Nobody is writing the countdown.

claim: Urdu is roughly 0.45% of language usage distribution across Pakistan's web and Urdu hreflang about 0.61%, against English at roughly 78.4%. Most users writing Urdu online use Romanized Urdu rather than Urdu script.
note: NEGATIVE FINDING that saves money: do not invest in Urdu-script content for business and tax topics. Measures sites, not searches, so it is directional.

claim: Under s.82(d) of the Income Tax Ordinance a Pakistani citizen may be treated as resident if not present in any other single country for more than 182 days, or not a resident taxpayer of any other country; residents are taxed on worldwide income under s.11.
note: VERIFIED against the Ordinance: see s82-residency-verified for the exact text. Correction: the primary presence test in s.82(a) is 183 days, not 182. The 182-day figure belongs to s.82(d), the other-country test.

claim: '+40% purchases in Ramadan, +76% at Eid, AOV ~$102' presented as Pakistani data
note: REJECTED AS PAKISTANI DATA. These are regional MENA figures. Pakistan evidence for the Ramadan/Eid cycle is qualitative only. Do not present MENA numbers as Pakistani.

claim: Income Tax Ordinance s.82: an individual is resident for a tax year if (a) present in Pakistan for 183 days or more in aggregate in the tax year; (c) an employee or official of the Federal or a Provincial Government posted abroad; or (d) being a citizen of Pakistan, is not present in any other country for more than 182 days during the tax year, OR is not a resident taxpayer of any other country.
source: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 s.82, amended to 31.07.2025
note: CONFIRMS the diaspora trap: s.82(d) can make a globally mobile Pakistani citizen resident even while living abroad. Note the (a) test is 183 days (substituted from 'eighty-two' by the Finance Act 2006), while (d) uses 182 in another country. Secondary sources routinely quote 182 for both. Supersedes diaspora-s82d-residency.

claim: No published per-keyword monthly search volume exists for any Pakistani tax, corporate or business query, in any free accessible source.
source: Exhaustive search across SEO-vendor blogs, Similarweb free tier, DataReportal Digital 2026 Pakistan, FBR/PRAL publications, academic sources
note: STRUCTURAL, not a search failure. Per-keyword volume is the core paywalled asset of Ahrefs/Semrush/Moz; they publish it in blogs only for keyword sets that market to their own buyers (US/UK marketing, ecommerce, AI). A Pakistan-geo tax keyword set has no such value to them. Only fixes: Google Keyword Planner with geo=PK (free with an Ads account), Search Console on a live page, or one month of Ahrefs/Semrush.

claim: Google Trends returns HTTP 429 from this environment on both the UI route and the JSON explore API, including via a warmed StealthyFetcher browser session.
note: Rules out relative-interest data as a substitute for volume here. Bing Webmaster keyword API requires auth. Recorded so this is not retried blindly.

claim: 7,496 unique real queries harvested from Google and Bing autocomplete across 30 seeds: 2,233 Pakistan-geo tax/corporate and 5,263 US-geo AI/dev. Files: research/keywords/pk-tax.jsonl and ai-dev.jsonl.
source: Google Chrome suggest API (gl=pk / gl=us) and Bing osjson, harvested 9 Sep 2026
note: Autocomplete is NOT volume. It is Google's own ranked list of common continuations, so it evidences real PHRASING and relative prominence within a topic. Reproducible: scrapling-py research/keywords/harvest.py <seeds> <out> --gl <cc>

claim: Of 2,233 Pakistani tax queries harvested, 453 (20%) carry explicit tool intent (calculator, check, verification, rates, slabs) and 219 are commercial. Highest-prominence tool queries include 'trademark registration check online pakistan', 'ntn registration check', 'secp registration check', 'pseb registration check'.
note: STRATEGIC. Tool intent is the largest non-navigational category and BarrioVibe ships 22 calculators. The four highest-prominence tool queries are all VERIFICATION/CHECK queries (NTN, SECP, PSEB, trademark) which BarrioVibe does NOT currently have tools for. That is a concrete, evidenced gap.

claim: Of 5,263 AI/dev queries harvested, 2,042 (39%) are commercial-intent. 'ai agent cost per month' and 'ai agent development cost' both appear at maximum prominence (rank 0 across many prefixes, on both Google and Bing).
note: CONFIRMS with independent evidence the earlier finding that cost is the strongest AI content opportunity. Also surfaced: 'ai agent vs chatbot vs llm' (a three-way framing nobody covers) and 'ai agent failure rate' / 'ai agent hallucination rate', supporting the failure-content cluster.

claim: fbr.gov.pk receives an estimated 4.1M visits over a trailing 3 months, 93.4% from Pakistan, ranking ~6,000 organic keywords, with top keywords being navigational: iris, fbr, iris login, fbr iris.
note: Vendor MODELLED estimate, not measured, with commercial incentive. Useful only as a demand-centre signal: FBR itself absorbs the navigational traffic. Similarweb dollar values beside keywords are CPC, NOT volume, and are easy to misread.

claim: befiler.com draws roughly 17% of traffic from outside Pakistan (US 6.41%, DE 4.09%, CA 3.79%, UK 2.38%).
note: Modelled estimate on a small site, so error bars are wide. Directionally supports the diaspora segment identified via s.82 residency (see s82-residency-verified).

claim: 5.9 million income tax returns were filed for TY2025 as of 31 October 2025, against 5.0 million the prior year (+17.6%); 3.6 million were filed with payment.
note: A hard administrative count, not an estimate. This is the realistic ceiling on filing-intent audience size in Pakistan, and the closest thing to a market-size anchor available.

claim: 'n8n: 1.5M searches, +833%' (Exploding Topics)
